North star: what this dashboard is for

Read this before any refresh or new feature. A change that doesn't help answer one of the questions below can wait.

The goals

  1. Investing. The clearest risk-adjusted long and short ideas across about 400 small and mid-cap biotechs, built the same way every month and scored against later prices, so the record is real and keeps improving.
  2. Buy-side healthcare ECM (Balyasny, Citadel). Know who will raise before the call comes: roughly how much, when, and whether we take part, pass or short into the deal.
  3. Gaps. Areas with many patients but no strong public drug, crowded areas where the weaker players get consolidated, and companies trading below cash.

One line: a disciplined, scored biotech process that makes better long/short calls and sees supply coming before the Street does.

The three questions we must answer best

  1. What kind of stocks did best and worst, in which periods, and what did we learn? → Record › What worked, quarter by quarter (any window, any factor), plus the frozen-call scoring and valuation principles.
  2. What are our top longs and shorts, and what do we see that the market doesn't? → What's next priority rows, and the Variant view line in every thesis: the odds (or sales) today's price implies vs ours, and why we differ.
  3. What are the key catalysts and likely raises over 6 months, how do we take part, and what would we tell the CEO? → What's next (catalysts, raise model, our view per deal) and the What I'd tell the CEO notes on every company card.

What I'd tell the CEO: the eight categories

CEOs are running the company; investors see the whole field, the tape and how holders price the stock. The useful notes are the ones a CEO can't easily see from inside:

CategoryWhat investors see that the CEO may not
Funding and timingWhen the window is open (run-up, runway, catalyst ahead), how big a raise, who should anchor it
How investors see youThe odds or sales the price implies vs the evidence, analyst coverage, specialist ownership
Where you stand in your fieldWho sets the bar in the indication, where the program wins, how crowded the field is
Strategic optionsPartnering to fund the pivotal, strategic review when the stock trades below cash, outside price anchors
Spend where the value isNarrowing spend to the program investors actually value when cash is short
Help investors underwrite youDisclose the numbers and the target bar, show full-population results, date the catalysts
Shorten or de-risk the pathBreakthrough designation, early end-of-Phase 2 meetings, an agreed path for a signal that worked
Launch signals investors watchThe metrics that show the ramp, guidance that bridges the market's expectation

The questions a fund will ask (and where the answer lives)

#QuestionWhere the dashboard answers it todayWhat's still missing
1What's your edge?Fixed rubric across ~400 names: efficacy vs a numeric bar, one valuation formula, honest catalyst dates, frozen ledgers (Companies)—
2Show me your track record.Record page: frozen calls scored vs universe and XBI, what worked by quarter for any window, what failed and what changedA portfolio, not just calls: sizing, daily P&L, Sharpe, hit rate, drawdown
3How do you size and manage risk?Inputs only: catalysts, PoS, runway, ours vs StreetPaper portfolio with sizing rules, XBI beta hedge, kill criteria
4Your top longs and shorts, and what's priced in?What's next priority rows; ours vs Street; variant view (market-implied odds vs ours) in every thesisOptions-implied moves and expected value per catalyst
5How do you underwrite a binary event?PoS, efficacy bar, Street gap, runway past the eventEvent trees (up/down move × probability) scored after each readout
6Who raises in the next 90 days, and do we take part?Raise model on What's next: size, month, our viewPast follow-on database (discount, warrants, size vs volume, 1/30/90-day returns, lead banks); shelf and ATM capacity
7How do you handle inside information from deals?Process answer onlyRestricted-list / wall-cross flags per company
8How much capital can this run?—Liquidity and short feasibility: daily volume, days to exit, short interest, borrow cost, crowding
9What did you get wrong, and what did you change?Record page: valuation principles, Sep 12 backtest, separately frozen model change—
10What's your sector view?Areas: cluster › area › indication › company drill-down, cheap/lagging map, crowded vs under-servedTakeover likelihood and deal comparables
11Can I trust the data?Frozen ledgers, logged input fixes with sources, scheduled refresh, rerunnable repo—
12What would you tell management?What I'd tell the CEO notes on every card (eight categories) plus our researched suggestionNotes written by hand for the priority names

Build priority (in order)

  1. Paper portfolio from the frozen ledger: sizing, beta hedge, daily P&L vs XBI, Sharpe, hit rate, drawdown (answers 2, 3, 8).
  2. Catalyst event trees with options-implied moves, scored after each event (4, 5).
  3. Follow-on deal database plus shelf/ATM capacity (6).
  4. Liquidity and short feasibility (8).
  5. Takeover-likelihood score and deal comparables (10).
  6. Compliance flags: restricted list and wall-cross log (7).

How to use this file

  • Every refresh: check the "What's still missing" column and move anything newly built into the middle column.
  • Every new request: say which question it helps answer.
  • Keep the honest version of question 2 current. The record is the first thing a fund will test.

Set Nov 24 2026. Update the table rather than the goals unless the goals themselves change.
